title: Invited: SambaNova SN40L: Unleashing Agentic AI with Dataflow
problem: AI inference clouds must efficiently support diverse models for interactive agentic workloads (LLM assistants, chatbots, agents) while maintaining high token generation performance during memory-bound decode phase and supporting rapid model switching at scale.
motivation: Token-per-watt efficiency during decode is critical for inference economics; model hosting costs dominate when serving diverse model architectures at scale.
method: The SambaNova SN40L uses a reconfigurable dataflow unit (a processing block where data flows through computation stages rather than repeatedly fetching instructions from memory) combined with three levels of memory—on-chip SRAM, intermediate-speed HBM (high-bandwidth memory), and DDR. This dataflow design enables aggressive compute-graph fusion (combining multiple computation steps into single super-fast operations), which maximizes performance during token generation (when the AI produces output). The three-tier memory hierarchy reduces the silicon footprint needed to store trillions of parameters.
key_novelty: The core idea is using a dataflow-based, reconfigurable processor (where computation flows through stages rather than fetching instructions) with a three-tier memory system to efficiently generate AI tokens and host multiple models.
contributions: 3x faster token generation vs. DGX H100
3x lower energy consumption vs. DGX H100
19x lower model hosting costs vs. DGX H100 through efficient parameter storage in HBM/DDR
